samples.summary: OfflineRuntime runs unconditionally on every authenticated route, adding a `GET /documents` request and creating the IndexedDB database even when the feature is dark
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute.tsx:35` now mounts `<OfflineRuntime userId={...} />` for every private route (`/d/:id`, `/s/:id`, `/p/:id`, `/n/:id`, `/b/:id`, `/documents`, `/w/*` — App.tsx:128-176). The effect at offline-runtime.tsx:59 is gated on nothing: it calls `retryPendingOfflineErase()` (:95), `new WafflebaseDocStore(...)` + `store.collectStale()` (:74, :107) which opens/creates the `wafflebase-offline` database, and `await fetchDocuments()` (:134) — a full cross-workspace document listing — on every authenticated mount. None of this is behind `supportsClientKey()` (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts:76, which is false at the pinned `@yorkie-js/react` 0.7.22 per packages/frontend/package.json:66) nor behind `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`. So editor routes that never listed documents before now issue an extra authenticated request per session, and every signed-in browser gets a new database, while the feature itself cannot store anything. The gate belongs on the new code (skip the runtime, or at least the store/listing work, when `supportsClientKey()` is false and nothing is stored).

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` changed from one request to three; its only production caller now triggers a full cross-workspace document listing before the destructive DELETE
samples.evidence: `workspace-settings.tsx:182` (`mutationFn: () => deleteWorkspace(workspaceId!)`) is unchanged, but `api/workspaces.ts:127` now runs `documentIdsIn(id)` first, which issues `fetchWorkspace(ref)` (`GET /workspaces/:ref`) and `fetchDocuments()` (`GET /documents`, backend `document.controller.ts:180-195` returns every document in every workspace the user belongs to, unpaginated) before the DELETE. `removeMember` (workspaces.ts:160) does the same whenever the removed id is the signed-in user. This is latency and payload added to a destructive action at a call site that was not updated or reconsidered; it also forced `api/url.test.ts:167` to weaken its "every request carries the encoded id" property to "some request does", which silently relaxes that check for every other route in the same table.

samples.summary: The share route's `NonDurableScope` guard is bypassed by the PDF branch, which returns before the wrapper; only the independent `pdf-` key exclusion keeps it safe
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentInner` returns `<SharedPdfLayout .../>` at shared-document.tsx:967-980 — before the `<NonDurableScope>` added at :1016 — and `SharedPdfLayout` (:753) mounts its own `YorkieProvider` and then `PdfCollabProvider`, which renders `CollabDocumentProvider` (`app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199`). That subtree therefore reaches the durability decision with `useDurabilityPermitted()` === true (the context default in `lib/use-durable-document.ts`), i.e. outside the positional guard this change introduces for share links. It is non-durable today only because `isExcluded()` separately refuses `pdf-` keys. If the PDF exclusion is ever relaxed, or this branch is reused for another type, a signed-in share-link visitor gets the durable branch — the exact case `NonDurableScope` exists to prevent. The wrapper should sit above the pdf/blob early returns.

samples.summary: The module-level `evictedKeys` map is never cleared on sign-in, so after a logout+login in the same tab the chip under-reports durability for previously erased documents
samples.evidence: `evictedKeys` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:~250-268) is a module-scope `Map<dbName, Set<docKey>>` shared by every store instance for the life of the page, and `dropAllForUser` adds every purged key to it. `rememberOfflineUser` (lib/offline-erase.ts:67-71) clears the *other* denial set (`erased`) when a user signs back in, but nothing clears `evictedKeys`. In an SPA logout→login without a reload, the freshly mounted durable client's first `appendChange`/`saveMeta` for one of those keys hits `refuseIfEvicted` and throws; that rejection reaches `onWriteFailure` in `components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:159-171`, which latches `writesFailing` for the whole open document — so the chip reports `Not saved` / `write-failed` for a document the SDK then repairs and persists fine. The failure direction is safe (under-promising), but the state is wrong and only a reload clears it.

mergedFrom.summary: Every 401 anywhere in the app now blocks on an IndexedDB erase before redirecting to /login

finding.summary: Any single 401 anywhere in the app now erases every live offline entry — including non-empty unpushed change logs of documents currently open — from a call site unrelated to the user's intent
finding.evidence: `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:250-267) calls `logout({ eraseLocalData: 'keep-archives' })`, which reaches `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` → `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser`. `dropAllForUser` (packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts, `dropAllForUser`) deliberately does NOT spare a document that is open (its own comment says so) and does not spare an entry whose change log is non-empty. Every other deletion path in this same store treats exactly those two conditions as inviolable: `evictOldest` skips any entry with `changeCount > 0` ("a non-empty log is work that may never have reached the server") and `collectStale` skips anything `isLive`. `fetchWithAuth` wraps essentially every request in the app — a notification poll, a sidebar `fetchWorkspaces`, the new `OfflineRuntime` `fetchDocuments()` — so a transient expired cookie or a backend restart, while an editor sits open with unpushed offline work, deletes the durable copy of that work. The inline comment at auth.ts:262-265 justifies it as "copies of content the server holds", which is true of the snapshot but not of the appended change log, which is by construction the un-pushed delta. Fix belongs on the erase call: the 401 path should spare entries with a non-empty log / open documents the way eviction and collection do.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. The finding says fetchWithAuth's 401 arm calls logout({ eraseLocalData: 'keep-archives' }) and thereby reaches eraseOfflineDataOnLogout -> WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser. In this repository: (1) there is no 'keep-archives' value at all — the option type is `eraseLocalData?: "all" | "none"` (auth.ts:34) and a repo-wide grep for `keep-archives` yields no source hits; (2) the 401 arm passes `eraseLocalData: "none"` (auth.ts:277); (3) logout() gates the erase behind `if (eraseLocalData !== "none" && res?.ok)` (auth.ts:134), so eraseOfflineDataOnLogout() at auth.ts:135 — the only non-test caller in the repo — is unreachable from the 401 path, and dropAllForUser (offline-erase.ts:31) is therefore never invoked there. The comment the finding quotes as justifying the erase (auth.ts:260-273) in fact states the opposite: it explains that the live entry carries the un-pushed change log and so nothing local is deleted on an involuntary 401. The other 401 path, fetchMeOptional (auth.ts:180-190), returns null without erasing. An existing test pins this behaviour: tests/api/auth.test.ts:119-126 drives fetchWithAuth against an always-401 fetch and asserts `expect(erase).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. The fix the finding requests is already the implemented behaviour, so there is no bypassing or broken call site to cite. Primary ground is not-present (the 'keep-archives' call site does not exist); the guard at auth.ts:134 independently makes the claimed path unreachable.
